e-4936.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(9,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $\mathbf{n}=3\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}+7\mathbf{k}.$
e-4936.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 9,-2,3 \rangle$ and the normal vector of the plane is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 3,-4,7 \rangle.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =⟨9,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,7⟩ & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z & =56 \\ 3x-4y+7z-56 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4937.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of the Plane Perpendicular To a Given Line
e-4937.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,4,8)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\dfrac{x+3}{-5}=\dfrac{y-1}{3}=\dfrac{z+2}{2}.$
e-4937.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle -1,4,8 \rangle.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\langle -5,3,2 \rangle.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =⟨-1,4,8⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $\mathbf{r}=\langle x,y,z \rangle$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,3,2⟩ & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z & =33 \\ -5x+3y+2z-33 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-2,3,-1⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨3,4,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨-2,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,4,-1⟩ & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z & =7 \\ 3x+4y-z-7 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,0,3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨2,0,1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =⟨1,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨2,0,1⟩ & =5 \\ 2x+z & =5 \\ 2x+z-5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-1,1,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=i+j+3k.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-1,1,-2⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨1,1,3⟩.$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ & =⟨-1,1,-2⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,3⟩ & =-6 \\ x+y+3z & =-6 \\ x+y+3z+6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,-2,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨1,-2,4⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨0,3,-5⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =⟨1,-2,4⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,3,-5⟩ & =-26 \\ 3y-5z & =-26 \\ 3y-5z+26 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-3,0,4)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨-3,0,4⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨3,-5,2⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨3,-5,2⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =⟨-3,0,4⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨3,-5,2⟩ & =-1 \\ 3x-5y+2z & =-1 \\ 3x-5y+2z+1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(8,3,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$\frac{x+2}{4}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z-2}{-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨8,3,-1⟩.$ From the canonical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨4,3,-1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨4,3,-1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =⟨8,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =42\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨4,3,-1⟩ & =42 \\ 4x+3y-z & =42 \\ 4x+3y-z-42 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(2,1,0)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=1 \\ y=-2+4t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨2,1,0⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨0,4,1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨0,4,1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =⟨2,1,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,4,1⟩ & =4 \\ 4y+z & =4 \\ 4y+z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
